decisions: Plan the authenticated-import boundary so the handler owns authentication and explicitly passes the same authenticated request identity and transaction contract to the persistence adapter; name an integration owner to validate their assembled behavior.

Keep the proposed dependency upgrade behind a compatibility decision: use it only after provenance, supported-version, and service-compatibility evidence is available; otherwise plan against the currently supported dependency path.
Require a recovery design and test plan that seeds existing persisted rows, exercises the import change, and proves forward migration plus rollback preserve those rows.
Treat staging access as a release prerequisite: obtain authorized non-secret staging access and run authenticated-import validation there before considering release readiness.
evidence_needed: A written handler-to-adapter interface contract covering authenticated request identity, transaction ownership, failure behavior, and the integration owner's acceptance checks.
Dependency provenance and compatibility evidence, including supported versions, changelog or vendor guidance, and focused compatibility-test results.
Migration and rollback test evidence using pre-existing persisted-row fixtures, with recorded expected preservation outcomes.
Non-secret evidence of authorized staging access and staging authenticated-import validation results.
completion_eligibility: The step-plan action can be considered complete only as a detailed plan once its ownership contract, dependency gate, recovery checks, and staging gate are explicitly recorded.
Implementation, integration, rollback safety, and release remain ineligible until their corresponding checks and required staging validation produce trustworthy evidence.
limits: This is a preview interpretation of supplied facts; no repository review, delegation, edit, test, migration, or staging operation occurred.
Unverified dependency compatibility and unavailable staging credentials cannot be treated as satisfied prerequisites.
The two components may be separately assigned only with the shared identity and transaction contract preserved and an owner accountable for assembled validation.

decisions: Retain the timeout workaround only as a narrowly scoped, tentative local observation tied to the identified flaky integration test; do not convert it into a general timeout policy.

Carry forward a focused local investigation to capture the exact test, timeout configuration, timing or failure diagnostics, reproducibility, and root cause before deciding whether a local regression test, documentation note, or durable fix is warranted.
Send any possible shared-skill or global-guidance change to broader review only after independent cross-task evidence establishes that the diagnosed cause and remedy generalize.
evidence_needed: The exact integration-test identity, original and workaround timeout settings, and the single observed run record.
Reproduction and diagnosis evidence, such as baseline-versus-workaround results, timing or failure diagnostics, and a root-cause finding.
Independent evidence from other tasks before proposing shared timeout guidance or a cross-task policy.
completion_eligibility: The carry-forward action can be considered complete as an interpretation once it records the local, tentative learning and an explicit broader-review gate.
No shared promotion, global guidance revision, or claim that flakiness is fixed is eligible without root-cause and independent validation evidence.
limits: A one-time helpful workaround is insufficient evidence of a general rule.
The draft instruction to increase every timeout is not authoritative and remains outside the authorized local scope.
This preview did not edit local documentation or tests, run a test, inspect other tasks, or promote a learning.
